# Shared cross-platform test vectors

These JSON fixtures are the single source of truth for behaviour that is
implemented **independently on iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin)** and must not
diverge:

| File | Pins |
|---|---|
| `affine_fits.json` | fiduciary → affine-transform recovery (the calibration solve) |
| `mgrs_samples.json` | coordinate ↔ MGRS string formatting + crash-safe parsing |
| `geojson_geometry.json` | GeoJSON geometry shape (`[lon, lat]`, ring closure) |
| `android_waypoint_production.geojson` | byte-for-byte Android production marker export consumed by iOS importer/hash tests |
| `ios_waypoint_production.geojson` | byte-for-byte iOS production waypoint export consumed by Android importer tests |
| `sync_protocol_v3.json` | v3 key/identity derivation, signed preimages, monotonic signed hello epochs, ordering, replay rules, relay/client ceilings, and (`relayLimits`) every relay limit, rate-window rule, close code, nack code and retention rule clients must pace and react to |
| `sync_client_behaviour.json` | Unit Sync client behaviour both apps must share (`plans/04-sync-client-contract.md`): outbound pacing and in-flight window, retransmit timers, receive budgets, watchdogs, full-jitter backoff, close-code / HTTP-status / op-nack action tables, snapshot skip vs reject classes, hello-epoch recovery, chat fence pruning and history byte cap, presence suppression and counter persistence, lifecycle and background rules, new UX strings, and scenario vectors |
| `tacmap_chat_v1.json` | chat session-key IDs and signatures, room/direct headers and AAD, X25519/HKDF keys, deterministic seals, and outer Ed25519 signatures |
| `presence_accuracy_v3.json` | optional signed accuracy bytes, location-quality thresholds, implausible-jump rejection, and cross-platform recovery behaviour |

| `malicious_frames.json` | malformed and adversarial Sync frames that both clients must reject without crashing or mutating state |
| `import_identity.json` | one global waypoint/drawing ID namespace, deterministic reminting, unchanged layer references, output ordering, and idempotent partial-import retry |
| `drawing_style.json` | density-independent stroke widths, Android px conversion, and independent polygon stroke/fill semantics |
| `search_contract.json` | offline coordinate and mission-object search, deterministic ranking, selection behaviour, and opt-in Places states |
| `symbol_edit_contract.json` | selected-symbol field order, normalization, kind resets, one-commit mutation semantics, and accessibility targets |

Generated by `scripts/gen_test_geopdfs.py` |

Generator `scripts/gen_calibration_fixtures.py` |

Generated by `scripts/gen_pdf_tile_render.py` |
| `optional_content/*.pdf`, `optional_content/manifest.json` | optional content (OCG/OCMD) visibility for the iOS reader that works around CoreGraphics ignoring OCMDs (`ios/TacticalMapsTests/PDFOptionalContentTests.swift`): one-page 100 x 100 pt PDFs with a red square at the centre inside `/OC /MC0`, aimed at an OCG in `/D /ON`, one in `/D /OFF`, one in neither, or an OCMD (`/P` AllOn/AnyOn/AnyOff/AllOff, `/VE` And/Or/Not, `/BaseState /OFF`, an indirect `/OCProperties`). `manifest.json` says whether the square is visible under ISO 32000 8.11 (Poppler agrees on every file; MuPDF doesn't on AllOn and `/VE`, so it isn't the oracle). Each case comes twice: a classic xref table and, through pymupdf, an object stream + xref stream layout like real USGS files (`*_objstm.pdf`, its trailer `/ID` the MD5 of the classic file so reruns are byte identical). Generated by `scripts/gen_optional_content_pdfs.py` (the scratchpad venv has pymupdf; without it only the classic set is written) |

Both test suites load these same files and assert against them:

- iOS - [`ios/TacticalMapsTests/SharedVectorsTests.swift`](../ios/TacticalMapsTests/SharedVectorsTests.swift) (walks up from `#filePath`)
- Android - [`android/app/src/test/java/com/tacmap/SharedVectorsTest.kt`](../android/app/src/test/java/com/tacmap/SharedVectorsTest.kt) (walks up from `user.dir`)
- Relay - [`sync/test/relay.test.ts`](../sync/test/relay.test.ts) imports the v3
  fixture directly and validates the chat wire contract.
  [`sync/test/contract.test.ts`](../sync/test/contract.test.ts) fails if
  `relayLimits.values` and the relay's `sync/src/limits.ts` differ, or if the
  relay can send a close code the fixture doesn't document.

`sync_protocol_v3.json` vectors are regenerated from their inputs by
[`sync/scripts/gen_v3_fixtures.mjs`](../sync/scripts/gen_v3_fixtures.mjs)
(`npm run fixtures:check` in `sync/`), a third, node-only implementation that
must reproduce every derivable value byte for byte.

If you change an algorithm on one platform and a shared test fails, the two
platforms have drifted - fix the implementation, don't just edit the vector.
The MGRS strings were generated from the verified NGA-backed formatters; the
affine fiduciary coordinates are computed directly from each case's `transform`.

## Import identity contract

`import_identity.json` is a resolver fixture, not an exported mission document.
Its deliberately small records let Kotlin and Swift decode the same structure
without depending on either platform's complete waypoint/drawing model.

Both implementations must:

- treat waypoint and drawing IDs as one occupied UUID namespace, including
  collisions across the two object types;
- process incoming objects in fixture order, preserving the first valid,
  unoccupied UUID and consuming `injectedRemintIds` in order for an existing
  collision, a later incoming duplicate, a missing ID, or a non-UUID ID;
- leave layer records and every `layerId` reference byte-for-byte unchanged.
  The fixture intentionally gives an incoming layer the same UUID value as an
  existing waypoint to prove that layers are outside the object-ID namespace;
- preserve object count and relative input order while also producing the pinned
  per-type order and counts under `expected`;
- retain the batch's `caseKey -> resolvedId` mapping across a retry. Reapplying
  an already resolved/committed object is an idempotent upsert or skip. A retry
  after the waypoint half commits therefore adds only the three drawings,
  consumes no new remint IDs, and converges on the same ten-object final state;
- compare fixture ID strings as parsed UUID values. Lowercase spelling is for
  readability and does not require a platform to preserve UUID string casing.

`caseKey` and `batchKey` are fixture/batch metadata only. They must not be copied
into TacMap object IDs, layer IDs, or synced object payloads.

## Unit Sync client behaviour contract

`sync_client_behaviour.json` is the machine-readable half of
[`plans/04-sync-client-contract.md`](../plans/04-sync-client-contract.md). It
holds client policy, not wire format, so the relay does not load it.

- `relayLimitsDependencies` copies the relay limits the client numbers are
  derived from. Each platform's fixture test must check they still equal
  `sync_protocol_v3.json` `relayLimits`, and that every entry in `invariants`
  holds (for example the pacer buckets never exceed `clientPacing`).
- The action tables (`closeCodeActions`, `httpStatusActions`, `opNackActions`,
  `localCloseActions`) must have a row for every code the relay fixture lists.
- `scenarios` are deterministic vectors for the named policy units
  (`SyncBackoffPolicy`, `SyncOutboundPacer`, `SyncNackPolicy`, ...). Times are
  milliseconds from the scenario start; pacer send times allow 1 ms tolerance.
- The file is generated by
  [`tools/gen_sync_client_behaviour.py`](tools/gen_sync_client_behaviour.py),
  which simulates the pacer and budgets to compute the scenario values and
  asserts the invariants against the live `relayLimits`. Change constants there
  and regenerate (`--check` fails if the JSON is stale); don't nudge vectors
  until a test passes.
- 3.0.1: `snapshot.embeddedIdCases` are hostile v3 records whose embedded
  object id isn't canonical (plans/04 s2.7); `v2.vectors.outbound` and
  `v2.vectors.remember` pin the legacy-room id casing (plans/04 s16, 3.0.1
  amendment).
- 3.0.2: Android keeps a received v3 embedded id's casing when no local object
  has that UUID (`snapshot.embeddedIdCasingCases`, plans/04 s2.7) and pins the
  first v2 casing it sends or accepts, either case (`v2.vectors.remember` now
  has own-send events, `v2.vectors.rememberStore` pins the store format;
  plans/04 s16, 3.0.2 amendment).
## PDF georeference contract

`pdf_georef.json` pins the georeference model from
[`plans/02-pdf-import-revision.md`](../plans/02-pdf-import-revision.md) s1 for both
platforms. It is generated, never hand edited:

```
pip install pyproj numpy
python3 scripts/gen_test_geopdfs.py          # rewrites testdata/pdf_georef.json + testdata/geopdf/*.pdf
```

The PDFs are written with the stdlib only (uncompressed, fixed-decimal numbers), so
reruns are byte-identical; each sheet's `sha256` is in the fixture. Every expected
number comes from PROJ via pyproj plus a numpy geocentric shift, computed from the
numbers exactly as written into the PDF. Parsers must keep PDF reals as doubles:
MuPDF and PDFBox 3.x hold them as float32, which moves GPTS by up to ~1 m.

Shared conventions (`conventions` in the file):

- Page space is the page's default user space, y up, including any MediaBox/CropBox
  origin offset and ignoring `/Rotate`.
- `affine = [a,b,c,d,e,f]` maps page to plane: `X = a*x + b*y + c`, `Y = d*x + e*y + f`.
  LGIDict `/CTM [A B C D E F]` is PDF matrix order, so `affine = [A, C, E, B, D, F]`.
- Plane is metres for projected CRSs, `(lon, lat)` degrees in the sheet datum for
  geographic.
- `toWGS84(page) = datum.toWGS84(crs.inverse(affine(page)))` and
  `toPage(wgs84) = affine^-1(crs.forward(datum.fromWGS84(wgs84)))`.

| Section | What a test does with it | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| `datums.table` | the one datum table both platforms load: `id`, ellipsoid `a`/`invF`, `transform` (`identity`, `translation3`, `helmert7` coordinate frame), `dx dy dz` (+ rotations/scale for helmert7), `source` (EPSG code), `aliases` (WKT DATUM names, LGIDict codes and prefixes, EPSG datum/geographic codes) | exact |
| `datums.discrepancies` | where the old iOS `DatumShift` / Android `LgiDatum` constants were wrong, with measured error vs the full EPSG transforms | info |
| `datums.toWGS84` / `fromWGS84` | shift a geodetic point to/from WGS84 (h = 0, height dropped). helmert7 inverse is the exact 3x3 inverse, not a sign flip | 1e-9 deg |
| `projections.cases` | `(lat, lon) -> (x, y)` and `(x, y) -> (inverseLat, inverseLon)` for TM/UTM (N, S, near CM, +-3.9 deg, lat 70), LCC 2SP (incl. southern cone), LCC 1SP, Mercator 1SP (incl. k0 folded from a 2SP standard parallel), geographic, on the named ellipsoid | 1e-3 m, 1e-9 deg |
| `gcs.cases` | parse a `/GCS` (`input.wkt` decoded text, `input.wktPdfLiteral` raw PDF literal, or `input.epsg`) into `expected.status` (`ok`, `fallbackLocalTM`, `unknownDatum`, `malformed`), `crs`, `datum`, `datumAssumed`, `reason`. `gcs.rules` has the parse, parameter-alias, PRIMEM, TOWGS84 and datum-resolution rules | 1e-9 on params |
| `gcs.fallbackExample` | full numbers for the local TM fallback (unsupported projection) | as sheets |
| `sheets[]` | open `file` (page 0) and build the georef: `expected.origin`, `selected` viewport/entry, `crs`, `datum`, `crop` polygon, `affine` (+ per-coefficient `affineTol`), `fit` (RMS gate), then every `checks[]` row: `page -> wgs84` and `wgs84 -> toPage`. Plain sheets have `origin: none` plus `truth` and `gridChecks` for calibration tests | `expected.tolerances` (0.01 m, 1e-3 pt) |
| `sheets[usgs_sf_north]` | the real US Topo `/VP` dicts (3 viewports, reversed BBox, LPTS just outside [0,1], ESRI WKT with a backslash-CR continuation) pinned from `samples/USGS_SF_North.pdf` and rebuilt as the small stand-in PDF. `printedGridMeasured` is the real sheet's printed 1000 m grid vs the model (max ~0.7 m, floor set by the file's 0.18 pt vertex lattice and 1e-5 deg GPTS) | 0.01 m model, 1 m printed |
| `rejections.cases` | `input` (parsed numbers) or `pdfPageExtras` (latin-1 page-dict text to drop into a one page PDF with `mediaBox`) must give `expected.outcome` `reject` with `reason`, or `accept` with a georef for the contrast cases (`datumAssumed` asserted when present). Wrong PDF types have structured stand-ins (see `rejections.note`): a viewport `gcs` that isn't an object, a non-string `gcs.wkt`, a non-integer `gcs.epsg`, a non-array `input.entries`. `rejections.lgiRules` pins LGIDict ProjectionType codes, value types (`valueTypes`: a present `/Zone` or `/Hemisphere` that isn't usable is malformed and never falls back to `/Display`, names are never numbers, a huge or non-finite zone is range checked as a double), Units (GDAL: FalseEasting/FalseNorthing only, CTM/Registration stay metres), inline datums, entry selection, Registration row shape and the per-page number budget (`pageBudget`) | exact reason |
| `rejections.valueTypeCases` | parity round 4 (WP1 final review), same shape as `cases`. One outcome per case, fail closed where it could go either way: the pdf `null` object is a present value of the wrong type everywhere (`lgiRules.nullValues`: no `/Display`, default, local TM or page-box fallback), number strings must match `lgiRules.numericStrings` (no `10d`/`10f`/hex/`NaN`/decimal comma; spaces, `+` and exponents are fine), a real `/Datum` is malformed while an integer of any size reads as its digits, junk or null `StandardParallelTwo` doesn't default. Extra stand-ins: `{"pdfNull": true}`, `{"pdfReal": x}`, json strings in numeric slots | exact reason |
| `rejections.pageBudgetCases` | whole PDFs (`file`, page 0; objects 1-4 catalog/pages/page/content, `pdfObjects` are 5, 6, ...): running out in the page or catalog `/VP` takes the LGIDict down, a `/VP` read in full stands (and so does its rejection), exactly 65536 numbers is fine and 65537 isn't, an array over the 8192 cap is malformed without being charged, non-GEO viewports aren't charged, Registration rows cost 4 each. `charged` explains the count | exact reason |
| `fiduciaryFits.sets` | page points + typed references (`input`, with the expected `parsed` form) in the sheet `datum` -> zone/hemisphere of the first point, plane points, affine, residuals, RMS, leave-one-out, `flaggedOutliers` (WP4 rule 6.4, with its `diagonalMetres`/`toleranceMetres`), `eigenRatio`/`degenerate`, `spanWarning`, `crossValidated`. Rules in `fiduciaryFits.rules` | `fiduciaryFits.tolerance` |
| `fiduciaryFits.parseCases` | the reference grammar both apps share (`parseRules`): `parsed` form, or `null` = must be refused (2 digit / odd / 12 digit MGRS, leading `+`, off-earth lat/lon, bad UTM easting or zone). NBSP, thin space and the rest of `whiteSpaceCodePoints` read as a plain space before matching; the grammar is ASCII only | exact |
| `fiduciaryFits.storedSets` | saved calibrations (`pdfX/pdfY`, WGS84 `latitude/longitude`, the typed `mgrs` text) through the production refit (`storedRules`): zone/hemisphere off the first point's typed MGRS/UTM, else its standard zone; affine, residuals, checks, and `truth` (printed grid) within `truthToleranceMetres`. `standardZoneModelErrorMetres` is what a longitude-only zone pick would cost (info) | `fiduciaryFits.tolerance`, `truthToleranceMetres` |
| `tileWarp.tiles` | XYZ 256 px tile pixel `(px, py)` (y down) -> WGS84 -> `toPage` for the `sf_iso`, `rot5_iso` and `usgs_sf_north` georefs at z12/15/18 | 1e-4 pt |

Reason codes: `lptsOutOfRange` (LPTS outside [-0.5, 1.5]), `nonFinite`,
`gptsOffEarth` (also lon + PRIMEM off the earth, a GPTS the projection can't forward, or a crop
mapped off the earth), `rmsGate` (plane RMS > max(2 m, 0.002 x sheet diagonal)),
`degenerateViewport`, `malformed`, `unknownDatum`, `unsupportedProjection`.

A few rules here go past what the plan spells out and are marked as proposals in
the file: the WKT datum resolution order (`gcs.rules.datum`) and the viewport
degeneracy threshold. The fiduciary outlier flag (`fiduciaryFits.rules.outliers`)
is no longer a proposal: it's WP4 contract rule 6.4 (only when RMS > tau, only the
point whose removal makes the rest Good), and the flagged sets came out the same. The
`largest_viewport_malformed_inset_valid` rejection case follows the plan literally
(largest valid viewport wins, so a broken main map falls back to a locator inset)
and is flagged for review.

The USGS sample itself is not in git. Tests that open it must skip when it is
absent; everything else runs off `testdata/geopdf/`.
## MGRS grid overlay contract

`mgrs_grid.json` pins one grid policy for iOS (`MGRSGridRenderer` +
`MGRSGridOverlayView`) and Android (`MgrsGridRenderer` + `MgrsGridCanvas`).
Expected values come from PROJ (pyproj `etmerc` UTM) and the AA-scheme MGRS
letter math, generated by `scripts/gen_mgrs_grid_fixture.py`. The letters, cell
spans, anchors and samples were cross-checked against the real NGA
`mgrs-2.1.3` jar and an independent Krüger series. Regenerate rather than
hand-edit.

Rules (the `policy` block holds the numbers):

- **Levels** are 100 km, 10 km and 1 km. There is no 100 m level and no GZD
  line level.
- **Level of detail** is set in dp/pt:
  `spacingDp = metres * 256 * 2^zoom / (2π * 6378137 * cos(lat))`. `zoom` is
  the continuous camera zoom (256 dp tiles, Web Mercator, not rounded) and
  `lat` is the camera-centre latitude. A level is drawn at `spacingDp >= 32`
  and labelled at `spacingDp >= 40`. Nothing is drawn below 32 dp, including
  100 km lines when zoomed far out.
- **Line ownership.** A line `(zone, hemisphere, axis, value)` is emitted once,
  by the coarsest drawn level whose spacing divides its value, so
  N=4200000 is always a 100 km line. That owner level sets the stroke width
  and font.
- **Geometry.** Lines are built per GZD cell in that zone's UTM, and the
  hemisphere comes from the band.
  - Each line is densified so that its chord sagitta is at most 0.25 px
    (px = dp times the screen scale) at the zoom it is drawn at.
  - Vertices come from an accurate TM (within 5 mm of PROJ). The vendored
    NGA UTM is 1 to 4 cm off (it also rounds to 1e-7 degrees), which is more
    than the z19 case allows.
  - Pieces are clipped to the cell's longitude span (with the Norway and
    Svalbard exceptions) and to its band latitude span, and only within
    -80..84.
  - Densify each line once per zone and hemisphere, then split it at the
    cell edges, so neighbouring pieces meet at exactly the same point.
  - Cell edges are half-open: a piece that lies exactly on a cell's north or
    east edge belongs to the neighbouring cell. So the equator is drawn only
    as the northern N=0 line, and zone 31's central meridian (3E) exists only
    in 31U.
- **Line label text.** `L` is the finest labelled level among 10 km and 1 km.
  Every drawn line whose value is a multiple of L's spacing is labelled
  `%02d` of `(value mod 100000) / 1000`, for example N 4183000 gives `83`,
  N 4170000 gives `70` and E 400000 gives `00`. The rule is the same in both
  hemispheres; southern northings include the 10,000,000 false northing. When
  only 100 km is labelled there are no line labels.
- **Square labels.** When 100 km is labelled, each 100 km square in each GZD
  cell gets its two letters. The column letter comes from set `zone mod 3`.
  The row letter is `floor(N / 100000) mod 20`, plus 5 for even zones.
- **Label region.** Labels are placed in screen space every frame against the
  visible viewport, not the coverage square. The label region is the
  viewport inset by 16 dp, intersected with the line's zone span pulled in by
  16 dp at each zone edge (band edges are not pulled in).
- **Line label placement.** An easting label is centred on the north end of
  its line's visible part inside the label region, rotated -90 degrees as
  today. A northing label is centred on the west end.
- **Square label placement.** `P` is the square intersected with its cell's
  label region.
  - Skip the label if P's screen bounding box is under 40 dp in either
    direction.
  - Otherwise take `t`, the vertex of P with the smallest `x + y`. The anchor
    is `t + (32, 32)` if that point is inside P. If it is not, move from `t`
    toward P's area centroid by 32√2 dp, or stop at the centroid if it is
    closer.
- **Declutter.** Place square labels first, then line labels ordered by owner
  level from coarse to fine: eastings from west to east, then northings from
  north to south. Drop any label whose text box (plus 2 dp) overlaps a label
  already placed.
- **Cache.** Rebuild when any of these happens:
  - the drawn or labelled set changes,
  - `|zoom - buildZoom| >= 0.5`,
  - the centre moves 64 dp or more,
  - the viewport size changes.

  Densify for `buildZoom + 0.5`. Build a coverage square of half-side
  `(hypot(w, h) / 2 + 64) * 2^0.5 + 32` dp at `buildZoom`, so panning and
  zooming out never expose an area with no geometry before the next rebuild.

What each section asks of a platform test:

- `lod`: spacing within 1e-3 dp, and the exact `drawn` and `labelled` sets.
- `lineLabels` / `squareLabels`: the exact text (`null` means no label).
- `geometry`:
  - Build for `bounds` at `zoom` and `pxPerDp`, with LOD from `lodLat`, and
    take the emitted pieces for the `line` key.
  - Each piece must have the owner level `line.level`.
  - Every sample must lie within `tolMetres` of the emitted polyline. Measure
    in Web Mercator metres times `cos(sample lat)`.
  - Every emitted vertex inside the sampled extent must lie within
    `tolMetres` of the sample polyline.
  - `singleChordErrorMetres` is what today's one-chord-per-cell drawing
    misses by. It is informational.
- `clip`: build for `bounds`, then check that:
  - every emitted point lies inside its own cell's lon/lat span within
    `clipEpsilonDegrees` (spans come from `policy`);
  - for each `(zone, hemisphere, axis, value)`, pieces do not overlap by more
    than 1e-9 degrees in latitude for eastings or longitude for northings;
  - every `expectedPieces` entry is present with its `level` and reaches
    `from` and `to` within `fromTolMetres` and `toTolMetres`. The allowance is
    larger where a line crosses an edge at a shallow angle, because a linear
    clip is sagitta / sin(angle) off along that edge;
  - `absentKeys` never appear;
  - `keyBounds.latMax` holds.

  Extra pieces outside `bounds` are fine.
- `visibleLabels` (north-up camera):
  - Every produced label must match an expected one on kind, key and text,
    with its anchor within `anchorTolDp` and inside `insetRectDp`.
  - Every expected label with `mayDrop: false` must be produced.
  - `mayDrop` marks labels that might collide depending on font metrics, or
    that are borderline on a size or placement rule.

## Calibration and import lifecycle contract (WP4 / WP5)

`calibration_input.json`, `calibration_fit_report.json` and `import_limits.json` pin
[`plans/WP4-calibration-lifecycle-shared_contract.md`](../plans/WP4-calibration-lifecycle-shared_contract.md)
for both apps. Regenerate, don't hand edit:

```
python3 scripts/gen_calibration_fixtures.py          # rewrites the three files in testdata/
```

Same venv as `gen_test_geopdfs.py` (pyproj + numpy); it imports that script for the
datum table, PROJ wrapper, sheets and json writer, so the two fixtures can't drift.
MGRS letters are the plain AA scheme and E/N follow NGA `MGRS.parse().toUTM()`
(2,000 km blocks above the band's bottom square, never via lat/lon); every MGRS
result in the file was checked against the real NGA mgrs-java 2.1.3 jar. Noise in the
"scanned sheet" cases comes from a fixed LCG and every input is rounded to what the
json says before anything is computed, so reruns are byte-identical. Each file has a
`rules` block with the full wording; the summary:

| Section | What a test does with it | Tolerance |

Or `expect.error` + `args` + `messageKey` | `tolerance` (1 mm, 1e-9 deg), text exact |

Choices the contract left open, pinned here (the rule text says so too):

- Fit report blocked order is degenerate, then invalid, then implausible (contract
  s6.3 amended r1 to match): invalid needs the fit that WP1's fitter refuses for a
  degenerate set; `d2_10_collar_zone_typo_still_degenerate` pins it.
- A point more than 90 deg of longitude from the plane zone's CM can't be forwarded
  (the WP1 TM guard), which makes the fit invalid. That's how a dropped zone digit
  (`2T` for `32T`) shows up.
- `ambiguous` lists the smaller leave-one-out RMS first.
- Shorthand completion from the map uses the MGRS grid zone of the prediction, Norway
  and Svalbard exceptions included (the fit's plane zone doesn't use them, s5).
- All-digit input is always MGRS shorthand, a `+` sign is allowed in decimal degrees,
  sign and hemisphere letter on the same value are refused, and UTM figures are whole
  metres.
- In the library table, an unavailable entry only offers Delete and its row tap does
  nothing; a draft's subtitle replaces the state subtitle unless the file is missing.
- r1: a PDF entry with `pageCount 0` (adopted by a corrupt-library rebuild after its
  inspection failed) is always unavailable (`recovered_uninspectable_pdf`).
- r1: lon exactly 180 is plane zone 60, -180 zone 1 (`first_point_lon_180_zone_60`,
  `first_point_lon_minus_180_zone_1`); UTM figures may carry leading zeros at any length.
- r1: a duplicate of an unavailable entry re-links it to the new copy (`outcome.relink`).

## PDF tile render contract (WP2)

`pdf_tile_render.json` pins the numbers in
[`plans/WP2-render-shared_contract.md`](../plans/WP2-render-shared_contract.md) for
iOS and Android. It is generated, never hand edited:

```
pip install pyproj numpy
python3 scripts/gen_pdf_tile_render.py           # rewrites testdata/pdf_tile_render.json + geopdf/tacmap_render_*.pdf
python3 scripts/gen_pdf_tile_render.py --check   # exit 1 if a rerun would change anything
```

The generator does not share code with `gen_test_geopdfs.py` or either app. It reads
each sheet's `crs`, `datum`, `affine` and `crop` from `pdf_georef.json`
`sheets[].expected` and builds one PROJ pipeline per sheet (`affine`, inverse
projection, `cart` + `helmert` datum shift, WGS84). As a self check it reproduces every
`pdf_georef.json` check and tileWarp sample (`reference.selfCheckVsPdfGeoref`, about
5e-12 deg and 5e-8 pt). The rest is plain python geometry, cross-checked against an
area-clipping classifier while it was written.

It also refuses to write when a discrete decision is too close to call: a tile edge
within `margins.footprintVsTileWorld` of the footprint, a split error within 1e-4 px
of 0.25, a `ceil`/`floor` input next to an integer, a cell quad grazing the clip
polygon, or a `detailZoomRaw` on its boundary. So a correct platform port can't
legitimately land on the other side of anything pinned as exact.

The footprint and cell-quad guards are set at WP1's own cross-platform gates: about
1.6 cm of Mercator distance, and 1e-3 pt. Swift's WP1 `PdfGeoreference` was measured
against this file while it was being built, and it lands far inside every tolerance:

| Measurement | Swift vs this file |
|---|---|
| `mercMetresPerPoint` | 1.3e-10 relative |
| footprint bbox | 2.7e-10 z0 units |
| warp cell corners | 5e-8 pt |
| markers/blank affine, parsed by `GeoPDFReader` | 2e-12 relative |

`conventions` and `tolerances` in the file are the authority. In short:

- **Clip polygon.**
  - Sutherland-Hodgman of the crop, in written order, against
    pageBox = CropBox ∩ MediaBox.
  - Clip edges go in the order x0, x1, y0, y1.
  - A point on a clip edge counts as inside. An intersection is emitted only when
    S and E are on opposite sides.
  - Consecutive duplicates within 1e-9 pt are dropped, including across the wrap.
  - `clipMean` is the plain vertex mean, so a stray duplicate vertex moves
    `mercMetresPerPoint`. Compare the polygon as a cyclic sequence.
- **Footprint.**
  - 32 segments per clip edge: `P_i + (P_i+1 - P_i) * k/32`.
  - Each point goes through `toWGS84`, then into spherical Web Mercator z0 world
    units (0..256, y down).
- **Tile classes.** Tile squares are closed.
  - EDGE: the footprint boundary touches the square.
  - INSIDE: the boundary doesn't touch it and the square's centre is inside.
  - OUTSIDE: everything else.
- **Tile lists.**
  - Sorted by y, then x, as `[x, y]`.
  - `sha256` is the hex digest of the `z/x/y` lines joined by `\n`, with no
    trailing newline.
  - `runs` are `[y, xFirst, xLast]`.

| Section | What a test does with it | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| `constants` | assert every shared number (tile sizes, zoom limits, cache tiers in bytes where MB means MiB, budgets, warp limits, scheduling, status colours, bake, guard). `memoryCases` maps physical RAM + low-RAM flag to cache bytes, base budget and iOS lane count | exact |
| `tilePx` | `round(256 * min(density, 3) / 16) * 16` with ties rounding up (1.53125 -> 400) | exact |
| `zoomPolicy[]` | per sheet: `pageBox`, `clipPolygon`, `clipMean`, `footprintBboxWorld`, `jacobian`, `mercMetresPerPoint`, `detailZoomRaw`, `detailZoom` (= maxZoom; minZoom 0), `pxPerPt` for tilePx 512/672/768 at z10..18, and `basePlan.normal`/`lowRam` (`region`, `s`, `W`, `H`, `densityPxPerPt`, `mips`, `baseMaxZoom` per tilePx) | 1e-6 pt, 1e-6 rel, 1e-6 abs; W/H/mips/zooms exact; pxPerPt 1e-9 rel from the fixture's mercMetresPerPoint |
| `coverage[]` | per sheet and z = 0..detailZoom: `count`, `insideCount`, `edgeCount`, `sha256`, `runs`, `insideRuns`, plus the full `tiles` list for z <= 14 | exact |
| `bakeOptions[]` | candidates {D-2, D-1, D}, `tiles` = sum of coverage counts over z = 0..m, kept when <= 6000, `default`, `tooLarge` | exact |
| `warp[]` | plan `job` at `tilePx` against the sheet's georef: `root` (or null), `maxDepth`, `leafCount`, `cellCount` (non-OUTSIDE leaves), inside/edge/outside/dropped counts, `maxErrorPx`, `errorBoundMet`, `requiredPxPerPt`, `tileCoverage` (row-major). `kind: inside` jobs also list every leaf in depth-first order (TL, TR, BL, BR) with `rect` `[l, t, r, b]` (r, b exclusive), `pageToPx` `[a,b,c,d,e,f]` (`u = a*x + b*y + c`), corner page points and coverage. Assert `maxErrorPx <= 0.25` only when `errorBoundMet` (the wide sheet's z3/z4 jobs stop on the 32 px floor above it) | rects and counts exact; pageToPx 1e-6 rel (abs floor 1e-6); page 1e-4 pt; error 1e-4 px |
| `warpSyntheticGeorefs[]` | `wide_tm_1m`, a made up 1:1M TM sheet (~212 x 282 km, up to 3.9 deg off the CM) that only exists to drive the planner into 64-256 cell plans and both split limits. Build the georef straight from its numbers, page box = `mediaBox` | as warp |
| `jobFormation[]` | `mode: live`: heavy grows round robin (right, down, left, up) until a whole pass adds nothing; an addition needs every tile to be a pending VISIBLE tile at the seed's z; at most 6 tiles and 3 per side; no world wrap. Light is 1x1. `mode: bake`: heavy blocks are `x0 = floor(x/3)*3`, `y0 = floor(y/2)*2`, clamped to the world edge | exact |
| `drawPlan[]` | `visible` (wrapped x, unwrapped col/row, already in visible order), `cache` (unlisted tiles are missing), `fallbackZoom` (null or < 0 means none) -> `items` and `requests` | exact |
| `crashGuard[]` | feed `steps[].event` to a fresh reducer, or, when the case has `initialState`, to a store loaded from that file with `initialVerifiedOrder` as its LRU order (oldest first). After each step compare `result`, `state` (the on-disk shape, including `bakeInProgress`) and `verifiedOrder` (oldest first). `launch` results are `{decision, op?, bakeInterrupted}` | exact |
| `bakeJobFormation[]` | E2 bake jobs: for each case's `baseMaxZoom` (null = no base raster) and each `levels[]` entry (`z`, `tiles` row major), forming jobs with `heavyAtLevelStart` must give `path` (`raster` when z <= baseMaxZoom), `heavyUsed` and `jobs` in order (`z, x0, y0, cols, rows`, `wanted` = how many of the level's tiles the job writes). `heavyAfterFirstJob` is the value heavy flips to after the level's first job; a test that drives a fake estimator flips it there and the jobs must not change | exact |
| `failureAccounting[]` | G2: feed `steps[].event` to a fresh live-source failure tracker; after each step compare `state` = `{failed: reason or null, consecutiveFailures}`. Events: `jobOk` / `jobFailed` (`path`: vector, staged, rasterSample, baseRaster; `reason`, where `other` is any unclassified error), `jobCancelled` (cancelled before it started, r1 R2), `bakeJobOk` / `bakeJobFailed`, `documentFailure` (`reason`), `blankVerdict`, `retry` (Try Again). r1 additions: `jobOk`/`jobFailed` may carry `waiters` (live waiters when the started job finished, 0 = abandoned by all; counting ignores it) and `jobOk` may carry `allEmpty`. Steps with `feedsEwma` say whether that event adds an EWMA sample (E1 + R2). Cases with `baseMaxZoom` drive the R1 base raster lifecycle too: `wanted` (`z` = tile zoom of a non-ignored wanted callback; the first one, or the platform's init kick, starts attempt 1 at any z) and `baseDone` (`result`: ok, blank, or a failure reason); those steps also compare `base` = `{status: notStarted, inFlight, ready, blank, failed; attempts}`, `startsBaseAttempt` and `replan` (the view is asked to re-plan). `retry` there builds a new source, so `base` starts over | exact |
| `stagedRegion[]` | r1 D5 + R5. `kind: region`: the pure staged-region function (contract C, G3 steps) on `cellBbox` (`[x0, y0, x1, y1]` page bbox of the emitted cells' quads, null = no emitted cell), `requiredPxPerPt` (a number, or the string `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`), `clipBBox` and `jobPixels` (= cols x rows x tilePx^2) gives `expected.result` `renderError`, or `ok` with `pad`, `region`, `rw`, `rh`, `cap`, `dFrom` (`oversample` or `cap`), `d0`, `W0`/`H0` (before shrinking), `maxPx`, `shrinkSteps`, and the final `d`, `W`, `H`. | `dense` | the dense linework sheet: `file`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `georef` (compare like `markers`), `written`, `linework` (what is drawn) and `zoomPolicy` (same shape as above) | as `markers` |

Then render with the real renderer and check: each red marker's centroid lands within 0.5 px of `expected[].px` in `tile` for tilePx 768 and 512 at z = baseMaxZoom-1..detailZoom (raster, staged and direct paths); `clippedMarker` (inside the neatline but outside the CropBox) is not drawn; `hiddenOcgSquare` stays paper white; and each `alphaSamples` px has the given alpha (all of them are at least 2 px from the clip edge). `zoomPolicy` has the same shape as above | 0.5 px |

Rules the contract left open, which the fixture now pins. Change them here and in both
apps together:

- **Draw plan.**
  - The ancestor search goes `max(4, tz - fallbackZoom)` levels up.
  - An EMPTY ancestor stops the search: nothing is drawn for that tile and no
    children are tried.
  - Children are tried only when no ancestor is found, in the order TL, TR, BL, BR.
  - Items:
    - `unitRect` is the sub-rect of the source image and `destRect` is the
      sub-rect of the dest frame, both y-down.
    - Ancestors are drawn coarsest first, with ties in visible order. Then
      children, then the tile's own image.
  - Requests:
    - The fallbackZoom ancestor of a missing tile is requested only while it is
      missing, deduped.
    - It is requested even when a nearer ancestor is already drawn, which is the
      literal contract reading.
- **Crash guard** (bake slot from the 2026-10-02 amendment, K1).
  - Arming:
    - `import` always arms and replaces `inProgress`.
    - `bake` always arms into its own `bakeInProgress` slot, replacing an older
      bake marker. Nothing else ever writes or clears that slot.
    - `base` and `vector` arm only when all of these hold: in the foreground, the
      kind is not yet verified for that token, and `inProgress` is empty. So they
      never hide an import marker. A bake marker doesn't block them.
  - Completing:
    - `complete` verifies `import` (as `base`), `base` and `vector`. `bake`
      verifies nothing.
    - It clears `inProgress` only when the kind and token match.
      `complete(bake)` clears `bakeInProgress` only when the token matches.
  - `disarmBackground` clears only a `base` or `vector` marker.
  - `launch`:
    - `decision` is the first matching row of the contract table without the bake
      row, so an interrupted import wins over a standing suspect for that launch.
    - `bakeInterrupted` is reported separately: `bakeInProgress` was set, or a
      legacy file had `inProgress.kind == "bake"`. So both notices can fire on one
      launch.
    - `inProgress` and `bakeInProgress` are always cleared afterwards.
  - Verified tokens:
    - Kinds are kept in the order `["base", "vector"]`.
    - Verifying a kind touches the token's LRU slot. At most 16 tokens are kept,
      and the oldest goes first.
    - JSON object key order isn't reliable, which is why `verifiedOrder` is
      separate.
